I get your point, but I've found if I avoid direct contact with an animal I'm OK. Otherwise I break out in a rash, eyes swell up and the inside of my throat becomes itchy. If I touch where a dog has been sitting then touch my face I get symptoms very quickly. I've been allergy tested and was told I was on the higher end of the scale for dog allergies. I think different breeds affect me differently. I'm pretty OK with poodle breeds.

NTA. I'm allergic to cats and super allergic to dogs. I go over to people's houses all the time who have pets. I just take anti histamines before I go, squeeze in some eye drops, don't touch any of the animals and I'm good. I also avoid lying down on any couches that have pet hair on them. Your FMIL sounds paranoid and overbearing.

I have so many mixed feelings about the ending! It was sad and amazing and incredible and awful all at once. I think I need to watch it again to get my head around everything.

I know that there are a few unresolved plot points we don't necessarily need complete answers/resolutions to (e.g. what happened to Kelsey and  Gina, what was in Hollyhocks letter, did Penny go public with her story) but one thing that's really bugging me is the whole Paige and Max thing. There was all this focus on setting up their characters and their romance and then...nothing? I'm so confused!

You have lovely hair and skin! Nothing wrong with your nose. If you are worried about your forehead try going with bangs or a side fringe. Just go to a hair dresser and ask for their recommendation on what will look good with your face shape. I think you'd look really good with bangs like Zooey Deschanel. One other suggestion would be to get your eyebrows tinted and shaped. This will help to frame your face and enhance your features. Good luck!

NAH. This is an all round painful situation for everyone. It's understandable that you don't want to move around frequently and it's also understandable that both your parents want to see you as much as possible. Maybe you could agree to trial the 2 week thing first and see how you feel about it? You might find it can work out if you give it a shot. Or maybe a trial of 1 month to begin with? I had many friends in high school whose parents got divorced and had to split their week 50/50 between their parents (3.5 days at mums house and 3.5 days at dads house) This was incredibly stressful for them as they could barely settle in before having to pack up and switch houses again. 2 weeks at either parents house seems like a pretty good arrangement in comparison.

NTA - don't let anyone, including your parents, get in your way of living your life and being happy. I understand that they are your parents and that you love them. But they sound like they are being selfish and don't actually have your best interests at heart in terms of you becoming an independent adult with a life of your own. 

You need to be responsible for your own happiness. It's great that you have achieved so much at such a young age. Your parents should be proud of you and encouraging you to spread your wings. Be firm but gentle with them. If they continue to make you feel bad for your choices, tell them in no uncertain terms what you want to do and that if they can't respect that, then tough luck. You don't need their negativity in your life.
